      Problem: The `%3N` format specifier (nanoseconds truncated to 3 digits) is a GNU date extension. It is not supported on BSD/macOS or other non-GNU environments.; The `date` command will exit with an error due to the invalid format specifier. In the workflow YAML steps, which run with `set -euo pipefail` (or `bash -e -o pipefail`), a failing command substitution causes the step to fail. In `scripts/review_apply_fixes.sh`, which uses `set -Eeuo pipefail`, the script would exit before reaching `exit 0`, breaking the editor success path. This can cause the review job to fail on non-GNU runners.

      Problem: GitHub Actions log command injection vulnerability - raw git diff --stat output is written to workflow logs. The output includes repository filenames which are attacker-controlled. If any filename starts with the literal sequence `::`, the GitHub Actions runner interprets the line as a workflow command. For example, a file named `::endgroup::` would prematurely close the diagnostic group; `::error::message` would mark the step as failed; `::warning::message` would emit a warning. This can corrupt diagnostic grouping or cause false job failures.; The GitHub Actions runner scans all stdout for lines beginning with `::` and acts on them as workflow commands. The diff --stat output prints filenames at the start of each line, so crafted filenames can inject arbitrary commands.

      Problem: git diff --stat HEAD shows only unstaged changes compared to HEAD. If changes have been staged (git add) but not yet committed, diff --stat HEAD will report no differences, creating a false "clean" diagnostic signal. This could mask the actual state of changes intended to be diagnosed.; If previous steps or Serena internals have staged changes (via git add or similar mechanisms), the diagnostic output would incorrectly show "(clean)" or "0 files changed" even though the index contains the editor's work. To accurately diagnose working tree state, the check should include both staged and unstaged changes.; ## HARDENING SUGGESTIONS
